title: How often does a 95 % interval hit?
intro: Draw n people, count the k who say yes, and build a 95 % interval for the true share p. The Wald interval p̂ ± 1.96·√(p̂(1−p̂)/n) is the one in most textbooks; the Wilson interval inverts the score test instead. Move n and the true p and watch the exact chance that each interval covers p. For a 95 % interval it should stay close to 95 %.
waldMeanLabel: Wald: average coverage over all p
wilsonMeanLabel: Wilson: average coverage over all p
plotTitle: Exact coverage of the two intervals for every true p (the jagged lines are real: k can only be a whole number)
